text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak telephones the Israeli president with condolences on the bombing in Tel Aviv of an outdoor cafe on Friday, in which four people died.
- U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen says that Egypt's role in the Middle East is essential for security and stability.

- Egypt will present a paper at the Islamic summit in Islamabad today on facing Israel's building of settlements in Jerusalem. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, on his way to Pakistan, makes a stopover in Muscat and presents a letter from Mubarak to the Sultan of Oman.
- U.S. vetoes for the second time the United Nations resolution condemning Israeli settlements.
- International Monetary Fund report says that Egypt's privatisation programme is proceeding with total success.
- International companies and investment banks are contributing investment to the Toshki projects.
- The sheikh of Al-Azhar says that all of Egypt is against the Judaisation of Jerusalem and settlement building, and is ready to sacrifice for the cause of Jerusalem.
- Turkey and Egypt discuss ways of increasing military cooperation, especially in the field of training.
